title: 'Who came today' shows one number but a longer list when a member checked in twice
what: Asking who came on one day gives a big number that counts different members, but the list under it has one row per check-in. A member who came morning and evening is listed twice, so the list holds more rows than the number says.
expected: The number and the list count the same thing: one row per member, with the number of visits beside the name.
how_often: any day a member checks in more than once
fix_line: For one day, group the check-ins by member like the multi-day list does

title: 'Plans ending this week' means 8 days on the Today idea and 7 days in the week summary
what: The Today idea 'Plans ending this week: N' and its list count plans ending from today up to 7 days ahead, which is 8 days. The week summary row with the very same words counts today plus 6 days. The answer card also says 'next 7 days' while holding 8 days. The owner can see two different numbers under the same words.
expected: One rule and one window for 'ending this week' everywhere, and the words say exactly which days.
how_often: whenever a plan ends exactly 7 days from today
fix_line: Use one shared ending-soon window and say the days in the label

title: History and the credits list show what the AI first suggested, not what the owner changed and saved
what: When the owner fixes a draft before saving (for example an expense of Rs 3,200 changed to Rs 2,300, or a new message title), the code note says the task is saved again as he left it, but only the AI's first suggestion is stored. History and the 'Recently used' credits list then show the old amount or title.
expected: History and the credits list show the amount, member and title that were really saved.
how_often: every time an owner edits a draft before saving
fix_line: Save the edited draft with the task, not the AI first suggestion

title: Tapping Shorter, More polite or Add Hindi throws away the owner's own edits to a message
what: After the owner edits a message by hand, the rewrite buttons send the AI's last words, not his edited ones, and the answer replaces the card. His changes vanish with no warning. The language switch already handles this; the rewrite buttons do not.
expected: A rewrite starts from the words on the card as he left them, or asks before replacing his edits.
how_often: every time an owner edits then taps a rewrite button
fix_line: Pass the edited words on the card into the rewrite, as the language switch does

title: A rewrite sends real phone numbers and emails to the AI company that the first request had hidden
what: Phone numbers and emails in the owner's sentence are hidden before the AI sees it, then put back into the draft. When he taps a rewrite button, the draft with the real numbers put back is sent to the AI with no hiding, so the privacy promise holds only for the first request.
expected: Every text sent to the AI, including rewrites, has phone numbers and emails hidden and put back afterwards.
how_often: whenever a message holding a phone number or email is rewritten
fix_line: Hide phones and emails in rewrite requests too and put them back in the answer

title: A plan extended by the assistant can be extended twice after a dropped connection
what: Payments, sales, enquiries and expenses saved by the assistant carry a once-only mark the server checks. Extending a plan and adding a member do not; only the open browser remembers them. If the save reached the server but the reply was lost, trying again extends the plan a second time.
expected: Every assistant save carries a once-only mark the server checks, so a retry never saves twice.
fix_line: Send the request id with extend and add-member saves and have the server refuse a repeat

title: The one-tap 'Record a payment' rounds dues to whole rupees, so a due with paise is refused
what: The 'Record a payment' button under a dues answer writes the amount rounded to whole rupees. For a due of Rs 1,499.50 it asks to record Rs 1,500, which the payment check refuses as more than is owed; for Rs 1,500.40 it leaves 40 paise owing.
expected: The button carries the exact amount owed.
how_often: only when a due has paise
fix_line: Write the amount with its paise in the follow-up request

title: A question about future dates gets a backwards range and shows zero
what: If the AI reads a question as a future period (for example 'next week'), the custom range is cut at today but its start stays in the future, so the card says something like '1 Dec - 25 Nov' with Rs 0 or 0 check-ins, which reads as a real zero.
expected: A future period gets plain words that there is nothing yet for those days.
how_often: when an owner asks about days ahead
fix_line: When the range starts after today, show a plain no-data line instead of zeros

items.reason: the assistant has no import or undo-import; it adds one member at a time through the same save as the form
